6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RigidityAffineReduction
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.PicEtAffZariskiSep
8	
9	/-!
10	# THE RING CASE OF THE `pic⁰` VANISHING IS ZARISKI-LOCAL ON THE TEST RING
11	
12	The surviving obligation of the whole vanishing route to a `JacobianData` is a statement at
13	an **arbitrary** `k`-algebra `A`, in either of two interderivable spellings:
14	
15	* `Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))` — consumed by
16	  `jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton` (`Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean:269`);
17	* ring-level field-point rigidity `hrigAff` — consumed by `jacobianData_of_rigidityAff`
18	  (`Pic0RigidityAffineReduction.lean:190`).
19	
20	This file attacks the **quantifier** rather than the content: both spellings are Zariski-local
21	on `Spec A`.  The input is the *separation* half of the landed Zariski sheaf property of the
22	plus construction, `PicEtAff.eq_of_away_eq` (`PicEtAffZariskiSep.lean:137`) — nothing is glued,
23	so the gluing half (`PicEtAffZariskiGlue.lean`) is not used.
24	
25	## What this is and is not — READ THIS BEFORE PRICING ANYTHING BELOW
26	
27	It is a reduction of the *test algebra*, not of the geometry, and it does **not** prove the ring
28	case.  Two things are load-bearing and were wrong in an earlier version of this header; both were
29	found by a fresh-context audit (`I-1657`, `I-1660`) and independently reproduced here.
30	
31	**1. AT A FIXED `A` the reduction is real: the ring case at `A` follows from the ring case at the
32	members of any finite covering family of localizations of `A`, and there is no route back.**  That
33	is what `PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away` and `rigidity_of_away` say, and it is the usable content
34	of the file.
35	
36	**2. UNDER THE OUTER `∀ A` IT IS NOT A WEAKENING AT ALL.**  The two `JacobianData` producers at
37	the bottom quantify their pointwise hypothesis over *every* test algebra — and
38	`Localization.Away f` **is** a test algebra, so the outer `∀ A` already covers it.  The converse
39	is one line with the trivial witness `f = 1`: `Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem` says `1 ∉ p`, and the
40	hypothesis at `Localization.Away 1` is an instance of the global statement.  So
41	
42	> `jacobianData_of_forall_prime_subsingleton`'s hypothesis is **logically equivalent** to
43	> `jacobianData_of_affine_subsingleton`'s (`Pic0VanishingRoute.lean:296`), and
44	> `jacobianData_of_forall_prime_rigidity`'s to `jacobianData_of_rigidityAff`'s
45	> (`Pic0RigidityAffineReduction.lean:190`).
46	
47	Those two producers are therefore **restatements, not repricings**.  They are kept because the
48	pointwise *shape* is what a local computation delivers, but a lane must not read them as having
49	reduced the obligation.  The general lesson, which cost this session a false claim: before
50	pricing a localisation-or-pointwise reduction as progress, try the converse with the trivial
51	witness — if it closes, the reduction only helps at a **fixed** base object, and the consumer's
52	quantifier decides whether that is any help.
53	
54	**3. The interface is NOT a local-ring interface**, contrary to what this header first said.  The
55	hypothesis is about `Localization.Away f`, and `IsLocalRing (Localization.Away f)` does not hold
56	(verified: instance synthesis fails; a basic open of `Spec A` is not a point).  A lane with a
57	genuinely local computation holds `Localization.AtPrime p`, and **nothing here bridges `AtPrime`
58	to `Away`** — that bridge is spreading-out, it is unbuilt, and it is the real remaining work on
59	this side.
60	
61	Seminormality is the other half of the story and it does not go away: see the measurement at the
62	end of this docstring.
63	
64	## The degenerate test ring: the site is not a counterexample, and that is ALL it is
65	
66	`hrigAff`'s antecedent is **vacuous** at a subsingleton `A` (there is no `k`-algebra map from
67	the zero ring to a field), so the hypothesis demands `q = 1` for free there.  That made the
68	subsingleton ring the cheapest potential *refutation* site for the affine spelling, and it was
69	recorded as genuinely unchecked (inbox `I-1655`, author addendum).  It is now checked:
70	`PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_subsingleton` proves the plus construction **is** trivial there,
71	unconditionally and with no genus or curve input.  So the site is **not a counterexample**.
72	
73	**CORRECTED after a fresh-context audit (`I-1658`), and the correction is the honest reading.**
74	An earlier version of this paragraph said this "settles the open question of `I-1655`".  It does
75	not.  At a subsingleton `A` the antecedent, the conclusion, *and* this file's own pointwise-local
76	hypothesis are all vacuous together — the section is the vacuous-hypothesis instance of
77	`PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime` below, since `Spec A` is empty.  So it tells a reader
78	nothing about whether `hrigAff` is inhabitable at any `A` with a **nonempty** spectrum, which is
79	what the `I-1655` addendum was actually asking.  Inhabitability stays open.  What the section
80	does buy is that a specific attack is closed, and the four steps below are reusable.
81	
82	The chain is four steps, each of which is about the vehicle rather than the curve: `Spec` of a
83	subsingleton ring has empty carrier (`PrimeSpectrum.isEmpty_iff_subsingleton`), hence so does
84	the product `C ⊗ overSpec k A` (project along `snd`), hence its Čech Picard group is trivial
85	(the landed `Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`, `Pic.lean:257`) and so is the
86	quotient `relPic`; and every étale cover of a subsingleton ring is again subsingleton, because
87	its spectrum maps *onto* the empty spectrum.
88	
89	## Main declarations
90	
91	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away` — **the reduction, `Subsingleton`
92	  spelling**: triviality of the plus construction at each member of a finite covering family
93	  of localizations gives it at `A`.
94	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.rigidity_of_away` — **the reduction, rigidity spelling**: the
95	  `hrigAff` clause at each member of the family gives it at `A`.  Note the direction the field
96	  points travel: a field point of a localization `S i` restricts to one of `A` by composing
97	  with `A → S i`, so the antecedent at `A` supplies the antecedent at `S i` and no lifting of
98	  field points is needed.
99	* `AlgebraicGeometry.subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_away` — the same reduction
100	  transported to the `pic0Subgroup` carrier the producers consume.
101	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime` — **the pointwise form, and the
102	  one a consumer wants**: no covering family in the statement, only a basic-open neighbourhood
103	  at each prime.  With `subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall_prime` on the `pic⁰`
104	  carrier, and `span_eq_top_of_forall_prime` as the `Spec`-level step (a mathlib lemma
105	  re-spelled, not new).
106	* `AlgebraicGeometry.PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_subsingleton` /
107	  `subsingleton_relPic_of_subsingleton` / `Algebra.EtaleCover.subsingleton_carrier` — the
108	  degenerate-test-ring chain, unconditional.
109	
110	## What was measured and did NOT work, so nobody re-runs it
111	
112	The obvious hope is that "local" is enough on its own.  It is not, and the reason is worth
113	recording: `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A)` **is** available for a local `A` (mathlib's
114	`CommRing.Pic.instSubsingletonOfFiniteMaximalSpectrum`), but the obligation involves the
115	polynomial ring, and `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial A))` does **not** follow from
116	`IsLocalRing A` — measured, `exact?` fails.  Traverso–Swan is the reason (that identity holds
117	exactly for seminormal rings) and a local ring need not be seminormal.  So at a FIXED `A` these
118	lemmas move the obligation to basic opens of `Spec A`; they do not discharge it there, and the
119	remaining content is seminormality-flavoured rather than quantifier-flavoured.
120	-/
121	
122	set_option autoImplicit false
123	
124	universe u
125	
126	open CategoryTheory MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
127	
128	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
129	
130	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
131	
132	noncomputable section
133	
134	/-! ## The degenerate test ring -/
135	
136	/-- Every étale cover of a subsingleton ring has subsingleton carrier: the carrier's spectrum
137	maps **onto** `Spec A`, which is empty, so the carrier's spectrum is empty too. -/
138	theorem Algebra.EtaleCover.subsingleton_carrier {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Subsingleton A]
139	    (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) : Subsingleton E.Carrier := by
140	  haveI : IsEmpty (PrimeSpectrum A) :=
141	    PrimeSpectrum.isEmpty_iff_subsingleton.mpr ‹_›
142	  haveI : IsEmpty (PrimeSpectrum E.Carrier) :=
143	    ⟨fun p => isEmptyElim (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A E.Carrier) p)⟩
144	  exact PrimeSpectrum.isEmpty_iff_subsingleton.mp ‹_›
145	
146	/-- **The relative Picard group is trivial over a subsingleton test ring.**
147	
148	`Spec A` is empty, so the product `C ⊗ overSpec k A` is empty (project along `snd`), so its
149	Čech Picard group is trivial by the landed `Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton`; the
150	quotient by `picFromBase` inherits it.
151	
152	Uses none of the curve's geometry — this is a statement about the vehicle. -/
153	theorem subsingleton_relPic_of_subsingleton (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
154	    [Subsingleton A] : Subsingleton (relPic C (overSpec k A)) := by
155	  haveI : IsEmpty ↥((overSpec k A).left) := by
156	    change IsEmpty (PrimeSpectrum A)
157	    exact PrimeSpectrum.isEmpty_iff_subsingleton.mpr ‹_›
158	  haveI : Subsingleton ↥((C ⊗ overSpec k A).left) :=
159	    ⟨fun x _ => isEmptyElim ((snd C (overSpec k A)).left.base x)⟩
160	  haveI := Scheme.CechPic.subsingleton_of_subsingleton ((C ⊗ overSpec k A).left)
161	  exact ⟨fun x y => by
162	    induction x using relPic.ind with | mk L =>
163	    induction y using relPic.ind with | mk M =>
164	    exact congrArg (relPicMk C (overSpec k A)) (Subsingleton.elim L M)⟩
165	
166	/-- The `A`-algebra map into a subsingleton `A`-algebra: everything goes to `0`.  Needed
167	because two plus-class representatives over a subsingleton base live on *different* covers,
168	and `mk_eq_mk_iff` wants a common refinement. -/
169	def toSubsingletonAlgHom (A : Type u) [CommRing A] (R S : Type u)
170	    [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [Algebra A R] [Algebra A S] [Subsingleton S] :
171	    R →ₐ[A] S where
172	  toFun _ := 0
173	  map_one' := Subsingleton.elim _ _
174	  map_mul' _ _ := Subsingleton.elim _ _
175	  map_zero' := Subsingleton.elim _ _
176	  map_add' _ _ := Subsingleton.elim _ _
177	  commutes' _ := Subsingleton.elim _ _
178	
179	/-- **THE PLUS CONSTRUCTION IS TRIVIAL OVER A SUBSINGLETON TEST RING**, unconditionally.
180	
181	This is a **non-counterexample only** (audit `I-1655`/`I-1676`): the subsingleton ring is the
182	site at which `hrigAff`'s antecedent is vacuous, and therefore its cheapest potential
183	refutation site.  The conclusion holds there anyway, so the affine spelling is **not refuted**
184	at that site — but this does NOT settle `hrigAff`'s inhabitability, which remains open on
185	nonempty spectra (see the module header).  It rules out one degenerate refutation, nothing
186	more.
187	
188	No genus hypothesis, no curve input beyond the standing section variable. -/
189	theorem PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_subsingleton {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
190	    [Subsingleton A] : Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) := by
191	  refine ⟨fun x y => ?_⟩
192	  induction x using PicEtAff.ind with | _ E ξ =>
193	  induction y using PicEtAff.ind with | _ F ζ =>
194	  haveI : Subsingleton E.Carrier := Algebra.EtaleCover.subsingleton_carrier E
195	  haveI : Subsingleton (relPic C (overSpec k E.Carrier)) :=
196	    subsingleton_relPic_of_subsingleton C E.Carrier
197	  refine (PicEtAff.mk_eq_mk_iff C).mpr
198	    ⟨E, AlgHom.id A _, toSubsingletonAlgHom A F.Carrier E.Carrier, ?_⟩
199	  exact Subtype.ext (Subsingleton.elim _ _)
200	
201	/-- The `pic⁰` form at a subsingleton test ring: a subgroup of a subsingleton group. -/
202	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_subsingleton
203	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
204	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] [Subsingleton A] :
205	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) := by
206	  haveI hplus : Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) :=
207	    PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_subsingleton C (A := A)
208	  haveI : Subsingleton (picEt C (overSpec k A)) :=
209	    @Equiv.subsingleton _ _ (picEtAffineEquiv C A).toEquiv hplus
210	  exact ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext (Subsingleton.elim _ _)⟩
211	
212	/-! ## The reduction: both spellings are Zariski-local on the test ring -/
213	
214	section Local
215	
216	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
217	variable {ι : Type u} [Finite ι] (g : ι → A)
218	variable (S : ι → Type u) [∀ i, CommRing (S i)] [∀ i, Algebra k (S i)]
219	  [∀ i, Algebra A (S i)] [∀ i, IsScalarTower k A (S i)]
220	  [∀ i, IsLocalization.Away (g i) (S i)]
221	
222	/-- **THE REDUCTION, `Subsingleton` spelling**: if the plus construction is trivial at every
223	member of a finite covering family of localizations of `A`, it is trivial at `A`.
224	
225	One application of the landed separation half `PicEtAff.eq_of_away_eq`: two classes over `A`
226	have equal restrictions because the target is a subsingleton. -/
227	theorem PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤)
228	    (hloc : ∀ i, Subsingleton (PicEtAff C (S i))) :
229	    Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) :=
230	  ⟨fun _ _ => PicEtAff.eq_of_away_eq C g S hg fun i => @Subsingleton.elim _ (hloc i) _ _⟩
231	
232	/-- **THE REDUCTION, rigidity spelling**: the `hrigAff` clause at every member of a finite
233	covering family of localizations of `A` gives it at `A`.
234	
235	Note which way the field points travel, because it is what makes this cheap: a field point of a
236	localization `S i` restricts to a field point of `A` by composing with `A → S i`, so the
237	antecedent **at `A`** supplies the antecedent at each `S i` — no lifting of field points along
238	the localization is required, and no compatibility between the members is used.  The classes
239	then agree with `1` after each localization, and separation finishes. -/
240	theorem PicEtAff.rigidity_of_away (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤)
241	    (hloc : ∀ i, ∀ q : PicEtAff C (S i),
242	      (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (φ : S i →ₐ[k] K),
243	        PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) → q = 1)
244	    (q : PicEtAff C A)
245	    (hq : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (φ : A →ₐ[k] K),
246	      PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) :
247	    q = 1 := by
248	  refine PicEtAff.eq_of_away_eq C g S hg (x := q) (y := 1) fun i => ?_
249	  rw [map_one]
250	  refine hloc i _ fun K _ _ φ => ?_
251	  rw [← PicEtAff.mapAlg_comp]
252	  exact hq K (φ.comp (IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A (S i)))
253	
254	/-- **The reduction on the `pic⁰` carrier the producers consume**: `Subsingleton
255	(pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A))` from triviality of the plus construction at each member of a
256	finite covering family.
257	
258	Transported through the affine comparison `picEtAffineEquiv`, then restricted to the subgroup.
259	Stated separately because `jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton`
260	(`Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean:269`) takes exactly this carrier. -/
261	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_away
262	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
263	    (hg : Ideal.span (Set.range g) = ⊤)
264	    (hloc : ∀ i, Subsingleton (PicEtAff C (S i))) :
265	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) := by
266	  haveI hplus : Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) :=
267	    PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away C g S hg hloc
268	  haveI : Subsingleton (picEt C (overSpec k A)) :=
269	    @Equiv.subsingleton _ _ (picEtAffineEquiv C A).toEquiv hplus
270	  exact ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext (Subsingleton.elim _ _)⟩
271	
272	end Local
273	
274	/-! ## The pointwise form: a hypothesis at each prime, no cover supplied
275	
276	The reductions above take the covering family as an argument, which is the wrong interface for
277	a consumer: a lane computing `Pic` locally knows something *at each prime*, not a finite cover.
278	This section removes the cover from the statement.  Two elementary steps do it, and both are
279	about `Spec` rather than about the curve:
280	
281	* if a set of elements meets the complement of every prime, it generates the unit ideal
282	  (otherwise it sits inside a maximal ideal);
283	* the unit ideal is spanned by a **finite** subset (`Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite`), which is
284	  the compactness of `Spec A` in the form the sheaf property wants.
285	
286	The localizations are then the canonical `Localization.Away f`, so no family of test algebras
287	has to be threaded through the statement either. -/
288	
289	section Pointwise
290	
291	/-- An indexed family of ring elements whose basic opens cover `Spec A` generates the unit ideal.
292	
293	**This is mathlib's `PrimeSpectrum.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top_iff` in another spelling**, and it is
294	written through it rather than re-proved — the audit finding `I-1659`.  An earlier version proved
295	it directly (a set in no prime is in no maximal ideal) because plain `exact?` fails on this goal;
296	`exact?` failing is not absence, and the mathlib lemma is stated as an `iSup` of basic opens over
297	an *indexed family*, which is exactly the shape the use site below has.
298	
299	Kept as a named lemma only because the `Set.range`/`iSup` translation is two tactic lines that
300	would otherwise be inlined twice. -/
301	theorem span_eq_top_of_forall_prime {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {ι : Type*} (f : ι → A)
302	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ i, f i ∉ p.asIdeal) :
303	    Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ := by
304	  rw [← PrimeSpectrum.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top_iff]
305	  ext p
306	  simpa using h p
307	
308	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
309	
310	/-- **THE POINTWISE REDUCTION**: if every prime of `A` has *some* basic open neighbourhood on
311	which the plus construction is trivial, it is trivial at `A`.
312	
313	No covering family in the statement: the witnesses are chosen at the primes, shown to span,
314	cut down to a finite subfamily by `Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite`, and fed to
315	`PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away`.  The hypothesis is about `Localization.Away f`, a BASIC OPEN and
316	NOT a local ring (`IsLocalRing (Localization.Away f)` does not hold); a lane holding a genuinely
317	local computation has `Localization.AtPrime p`, and the `AtPrime`-to-`Away` bridge is spreading
318	out and is unbuilt.  So this is the interface for a computation over basic opens, which is a
319	weaker thing than the header of this file originally claimed. -/
320	theorem PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime
321	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
322	      Subsingleton (PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f))) :
323	    Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) := by
324	  classical
325	  choose f hf hsub using h
326	  have hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ :=
327	    span_eq_top_of_forall_prime f fun p => ⟨p, hf p⟩
328	  obtain ⟨t, hts, ht⟩ := (Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite (Set.range f)).mp hspan
329	  refine PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_away C (ι := {x // x ∈ t}) (fun i => i.1)
330	    (fun i => Localization.Away i.1) ?_ ?_
331	  · rwa [show (Set.range fun i : {x // x ∈ t} => i.1) = (↑t : Set A) from by
332	      ext x; exact ⟨fun ⟨i, hi⟩ => hi ▸ i.2, fun hx => ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, rfl⟩⟩]
333	  · intro i
334	    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hts i.2
335	    exact hp ▸ hsub p
336	
337	/-- The pointwise reduction on the `pic⁰` carrier the producers consume. -/
338	theorem subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall_prime
339	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
340	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
341	      Subsingleton (PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f))) :
342	    Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k A)) := by
343	  haveI hplus : Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A) :=
344	    PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime C h
345	  haveI : Subsingleton (picEt C (overSpec k A)) :=
346	    @Equiv.subsingleton _ _ (picEtAffineEquiv C A).toEquiv hplus
347	  exact ⟨fun s t => Subtype.ext (Subsingleton.elim _ _)⟩
348	
349	/-- **THE POINTWISE REDUCTION, rigidity spelling**: the `hrigAff` clause at a basic open around
350	each prime gives it at `A`.
351	
352	Same three steps as `PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime` (choose, span, cut to finite), fed
353	to `PicEtAff.rigidity_of_away`.  Stated separately because `jacobianData_of_rigidityAff`
354	consumes the rigidity clause and not a `Subsingleton`, and because the rigidity form is the one
355	that carries no degree apparatus. -/
356	theorem PicEtAff.rigidity_of_forall_prime
357	    (h : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
358	      ∀ q : PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f),
359	        (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (φ : Localization.Away f →ₐ[k] K),
360	          PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) → q = 1)
361	    (q : PicEtAff C A)
362	    (hq : ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (φ : A →ₐ[k] K),
363	      PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) :
364	    q = 1 := by
365	  classical
366	  choose f hf hrig using h
367	  have hspan : Ideal.span (Set.range f) = ⊤ :=
368	    span_eq_top_of_forall_prime f fun p => ⟨p, hf p⟩
369	  obtain ⟨t, hts, ht⟩ := (Ideal.span_eq_top_iff_finite (Set.range f)).mp hspan
370	  refine PicEtAff.rigidity_of_away C (ι := {x // x ∈ t}) (fun i => i.1)
371	    (fun i => Localization.Away i.1) ?_ ?_ q hq
372	  · rwa [show (Set.range fun i : {x // x ∈ t} => i.1) = (↑t : Set A) from by
373	      ext x; exact ⟨fun ⟨i, hi⟩ => hi ▸ i.2, fun hx => ⟨⟨x, hx⟩, rfl⟩⟩]
374	  · intro i
375	    obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := hts i.2
376	    exact hp ▸ hrig p
377	
378	end Pointwise
379	
380	/-! ## The composition to the goal object
381	
382	The reductions above are worth nothing if they do not reach `JacobianData`.  These two
383	declarations are that check, and they are what makes this file usable by the representability
384	headline rather than local to its own row: the *pointwise-local* hypothesis, quantified over
385	every test algebra, produces the datum through the landed producers with no atlas, no chart
386	certificate, no coverage clause, no divisor representability and no rational point.
387	
388	Both carry the genus-`0` hypothesis of the producer they compose with, and neither adds anything
389	else. -/
390	
391	section Datum
392	
393	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
394	
395	/-- **`JacobianData` from the pointwise-local vanishing.**
396	
397	`subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall_prime` at every test algebra, fed to
398	`jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton` (`Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean:269`).  The
399	hypothesis mentions no test object, no open and no morphism of schemes: only `k`-algebras, their
400	primes, and the plus construction at the canonical localizations. -/
401	def jacobianData_of_forall_prime_subsingleton
402	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A],
403	      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
404	        Subsingleton (PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f))) :
405	    JacobianData C :=
406	  jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton C fun A _ _ =>
407	    subsingleton_pic0Subgroup_overSpec_of_forall_prime C (h A)
408	
409	/-- **`JacobianData` from the pointwise-local rigidity**, at genus `0`.
410	
411	The rigidity analogue, through `jacobianData_of_rigidityAff`
412	(`Pic0RigidityAffineReduction.lean:190`).  This is the shortest statement of the whole vanishing
413	route's remaining debt IN SHAPE, though — per point 2 of the module docstring — not in
414	strength: this hypothesis is logically equivalent to `jacobianData_of_rigidityAff`'s own. -/
415	def jacobianData_of_forall_prime_rigidity (hg : genus C = 0)
416	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A],
417	      ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
418	        ∀ q : PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f),
419	          (∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (φ : Localization.Away f →ₐ[k] K),
420	            PicEtAff.mapAlg C φ q = 1) → q = 1) :
421	    JacobianData C :=
422	  jacobianData_of_rigidityAff C hg fun A _ _ => PicEtAff.rigidity_of_forall_prime C (h A)
423	
424	/-! ### The equivalence, proved rather than asserted
425	
426	Point 2 of the module docstring says the two producers above are restatements.  A docstring
427	saying so is a claim nobody checks, so here it is as a theorem: the converse direction, with the
428	trivial witness `f = 1`.  Together with `PicEtAff.subsingleton_of_forall_prime` (which is the
429	forward direction) the two hypotheses are interderivable, and the same argument works verbatim for
430	the rigidity spelling.
431	
432	This is the check that should be run on *any* localisation-or-pointwise reduction before it is
433	priced as progress. -/
434	
435	omit [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] in
436	/-- **The converse, with the trivial witness**: the global hypothesis implies the pointwise-local
437	one, because `Localization.Away 1` is itself a test algebra and `1` lies outside every prime.
438	
439	So under the outer `∀ A` the pointwise form is *not* weaker — the content of the audit finding
440	`I-1660`, kept in the file so the equivalence cannot be lost again. -/
441	theorem forall_prime_subsingleton_of_forall
442	    (h : ∀ (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A], Subsingleton (PicEtAff C A))
443	    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Algebra k A] (p : PrimeSpectrum A) :
444	    ∃ f : A, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧ Subsingleton (PicEtAff C (Localization.Away f)) :=
445	  ⟨1, fun hc => p.isPrime.ne_top (Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem _ hc isUnit_one),
446	    h (Localization.Away (1 : A))⟩
447	
448	end Datum
449	
450	end
451	
452	end AlgebraicGeometry
453

events.text: This is a large, well-mapped effort. My claim I-1710 (the Laurent scheme bridge) is announced. The key file for the real gap (étale-plus honesty) is the engine file. Let me read it and the relevant relPic/picEt definitions in parallel.

1	/-

4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
5	-/
6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RingFibrewiseTrivial
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0RingDatumEngine
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafExtraction
9	
10	/-!
11	# THE RIGID ENGINE FIRES FROM A `pic⁰` MEMBERSHIP, WITH NO FIBREWISE BINDER LEFT
12	
13	`Picard/Pic0RingDatumEngine.lean` fires the RE-4 rigid engine at genus `0` on a
14	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π` under the fibrewise binder
15	
16	  `htriv : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum B, (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1`
17	
18	and `Picard/Pic0RingFibrewiseTrivial.lean` proves the corresponding statement for a class in
19	`pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B)`.  **This file joins the two**: for a cocycle-presented `pic⁰`
20	class the binder is discharged, so the engine's conclusions hold with no fibrewise hypothesis
21	anywhere in the statement.
22	
23	## What had to be written, and why it is not a restatement
24	
25	Three spelling seams, each of which had to be crossed rather than asserted:
26	
27	1. **`relCurveMap` vs the whiskering.**  The engine's base-change naturality
28	   (`cechPicClass_baseChange`) is stated on `relCurveMap C B B'`, which is *defined* as
29	   `(C ◁ overSpecMap B B').left` (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:160`); the degree
30	   seam (`Picard/DegreeSeam.lean:81`) is stated on `(C ◁ Over.overSpecMap φ).left`.  The two
31	   `overSpecMap`s are **independent definitions in different namespaces** — the duplicate pair
32	   recorded as `I-0144` — and they agree by `rfl` only when `φ` is the canonical algebra map
33	   `(Algebra.ofId B κ(p)).restrictScalars k`.  `relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` is
34	   that identification, and everything downstream needs it.
35	2. **Field points vs primes.**  `pic0Subgroup` membership quantifies over `k`-algebra maps
36	   into fields; the engine quantifies over `PrimeSpectrum B`.  A residue field *is* such a
37	   field but the instantiation is a written step, not an observation.
38	3. **Degree vs triviality.**  What the membership gives at a prime is a vanishing `classDeg`;
39	   what the engine wants is a trivial class.  The engine's own
40	   `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts one to the other at genus `0`, and
41	   it carries **five fibre instance binders** that do not synthesize through the `relCurve`
42	   `def` barrier; they are installed by hand here, as they are there.
43	
44	## What this buys, stated exactly
45	
46	The remaining distance from a `pic⁰` class over a test ring to *triviality* of that class is
47	now: `H¹(C_B, F) = 0` and `H⁰(C_B, F)` invertible (stalk rank `1` at every prime) **are
48	available**, unconditionally on the class beyond its being degree-zero and presented.  On the
49	**divisor/pushforward route** the step that turns an invertible pushforward into a
50	trivialization of the class is the evaluation map `π^*π_*L → L`, which my search did not find in
51	this tree.
52	
53	**Scope corrected after review.**  An earlier version of this paragraph called that evaluation
54	map "the remaining step" for the ring case as such, and asserted its absence from the sibling
55	project and mathlib as measured.  Both were too strong.  It is the remaining step on *this*
56	route only: `Picard/Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` reaches the same vanishing through
57	field-point rigidity, which never produces a divisor and so never needs the evaluation map at
58	all.  And I verified absence only in AJCR — not in `Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, which has
59	adjunction/counit material, and not in mathlib.
60	
61	## What this does NOT do
62	
63	* **It does not prove the ring case**, and it is not on the shortest route to it.  The
64	  evaluation step above is not built here; a fibrewise-trivial class over a ring need not be
65	  trivial (Traverso–Swan: `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial A))` fails even *given*
66	  `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A)`, measured).  A lane wanting only the vanishing should read
67	  `Pic0VanishingRigidityReduction.lean` first: it reduces the same goal to field-point rigidity
68	  with no cohomology, no pushforward and no divisor.  What *this* file is for is the
69	  pushforward route, where `π_*L` invertible is the object of interest in its own right.
70	* **`IsNoetherianRing B` is inherited**, not introduced: it is the engine's own binder, which
71	  `Cohomology/DatumDescent.lean:547` is designed to remove.  Nothing here re-proves it and a
72	  consumer should remove it through that route.
73	* **The cocycle presentation is a real hypothesis** on the `pic⁰` class, inherited from the
74	  DAT-4 degree seam.  `exists_cechPicClass_eq` produces a datum for any Čech class on `C_B`,
75	  but relating *that* datum's class to the plus-class presentation of a `picEt` element is the
76	  `picEtAffineEquiv`/`unit` seam, and it is assumed here rather than proved.
77	
78	  **What the binder is, exactly, after measurement — and a first answer CORRECTED.**  The
79	  *datum* half is free: `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` below produces a presenting datum for
80	  any class whose affine collapse is `PicEtAff.unit` of *some* relative class (`relPicMk` is
81	  surjective and `exists_cechPicClass_eq` is total over every `k`-algebra).
82	
83	  An earlier version of this paragraph then named ring-level surjectivity of `PicEtAff.unit` as
84	  the remaining brick, on the ground that `PicEtAff.unit_surjective_of_section`
85	  (`Picard/EffectivityClose.lean:141`) is field-only and section-dependent.  **That was wrong**,
86	  and a fresh-context audit caught it: `picEtAffineEquiv_relPicToPicEt`
87	  (`Picard/PicEtUnit.lean:161`) supplies the seam at an **arbitrary test ring**, with no field,
88	  no section and no curve hypothesis, for every class in the range of `relPicToPicEt`.  So the
89	  seam is not the obstruction it was priced as; `presentation_of_relPicToPicEt` below is that
90	  observation made usable, and `rigidEngine_of_relPicToPicEt` fires the engine with the
91	  presentation binder **eliminated** for such classes.
92	
93	  What is genuinely missing is therefore **surjectivity of `relPicToPicEt` onto `picEt`** — that
94	  every étale-plus class over a ring comes from a relative Picard class — which is a different
95	  statement about a different map, and is what a lane wanting these conclusions at an
96	  *arbitrary* degree-zero class should target.  `Pic0ChartPlusFibreProducer.lean:199` calls
97	  membership in that range "honesty" and treats it as a real condition, which is consistent.
98	* **Genus `0` only.**  At positive genus the fibre classes are not trivial.
99	
100	## Main declarations
101	
102	* `AlgebraicGeometry.relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField` — the `I-0144` spelling bridge.
103	* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_datum_relPicMk_eq` / `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` — the datum in
104	  the presentation binder is produced, not assumed, at every test ring.
105	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.htriv_of_pic0` — **the discharge**: the engine's
106	  fibrewise binder, from a cocycle-presented `pic⁰` class.
107	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rigidEngine_of_pic0` — the engine's three
108	  conclusions with no fibrewise hypothesis.
109	* `AlgebraicGeometry.BasicOpenCocycleDatum.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` —
110	  **`π_*L` invertible** from a `pic⁰` membership.
111	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.rankAtStalk_hModule_zero_eq_one_of_pic0` — non-vacuity at `ℙ¹` over an
112	  arbitrary field.
113	-/
114	
115	set_option autoImplicit false
116	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
117	
118	universe u
119	
120	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
121	
122	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
123	
124	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
125	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
126	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
127	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
128	
129	noncomputable section
130	
131	/-! ## The spelling bridge (`I-0144`) -/
132	
133	/-- **The two `overSpecMap`s agree at a residue field.**
134	
135	`overSpecMap B κ(p)` (`Cohomology/RelativeSectionsLinear.lean:147`) is built from the
136	`algebraMap`; `Over.overSpecMap φ` (`Picard/RelPicAlgebra.lean:44`) from an arbitrary
137	`k`-algebra map.  These are two independent definitions of the same morphism in different
138	namespaces — the duplicate pair filed as `I-0144` — and at the canonical map
139	`(Algebra.ofId B κ(p)).restrictScalars k` they are definitionally equal.
140	
141	Stated because the engine's base-change lemmas live on the first spelling and the degree seam
142	on the second, so no composition of the two is possible without it. -/
143	theorem relCurveMap_eq_whiskerLeft_residueField (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
144	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
145	    relCurveMap C B p.asIdeal.ResidueField
146	      = (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap
147	          ((Algebra.ofId B p.asIdeal.ResidueField).restrictScalars k)).left :=
148	  rfl
149	
150	/-! ## The datum in the presentation binder is not a real constraint -/
151	
152	/-- **Every relative Picard class over a test ring is presented by a cocycle datum.**
153	
154	`relPicMk` is surjective (`RelPic.lean:75`) and `exists_cechPicClass_eq`
155	(`Cohomology/GluedSheafExtraction.lean:301`) turns the resulting Čech class into a
156	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum` with the same class, at **every** `k`-algebra `B`.
157	
158	This is what makes the presentation binder of the theorems below a condition on the *class*
159	rather than on a choice of datum: a `pic⁰` class that is `PicEtAff.unit` of some relative class
160	at all is presented by some datum, and `exists_datum_pic0_presentation` extracts it. -/
161	theorem exists_datum_relPicMk_eq (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
162	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
163	    (z : relPic C (overSpec k B)) :
164	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π, relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass = z := by
165	  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ := relPicMk_surjective C (overSpec k B) z
166	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq (π := π) L
167	  exact ⟨D, by rw [hD, hL]⟩
168	
169	/-- **The presentation binder, in its weakest form**: if the affine collapse of `lam` is
170	`PicEtAff.unit` of *any* relative class, then it is `PicEtAff.unit` of `relPicMk` of some
171	datum's Čech class — which is the hypothesis the theorems below take.
172	
173	So those theorems do not secretly quantify over a lucky datum: the datum is produced, and the
174	surviving hypothesis is the `picEtAffineEquiv`/`unit` seam on `lam` alone. -/
175	theorem exists_datum_pic0_presentation (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
176	    (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra k B] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]
177	    (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
178	    (h : ∃ z : relPic C (overSpec k B), picEtAffineEquiv C B lam = PicEtAff.unit C B z) :
179	    ∃ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
180	      picEtAffineEquiv C B lam
181	        = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass) := by
182	  obtain ⟨z, hz⟩ := h
183	  obtain ⟨D, hD⟩ := exists_datum_relPicMk_eq C B π z
184	  exact ⟨D, by rw [hz, hD]⟩
185	
186	namespace BasicOpenCocycleDatum
187	
188	/-! ## The fibrewise binder, discharged -/
189	
190	/-- **THE DISCHARGE**: the engine's fibrewise binder holds for a cocycle-presented `pic⁰`
191	class, at genus `0`.
192	
193	Composition of three landed steps and the bridge above:
194	`cechPicClass_baseChange` moves the fibre class onto `Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap …)`;
195	the bridge rewrites that as the whiskering the degree seam speaks about;
196	`classDeg_fibre_eq_zero_of_cocyclePresented` gives `classDeg κ(p) = 0` from the membership;
197	and the engine's `fibre_cechPicClass_eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero` converts degree `0` to
198	triviality at genus `0`.
199	
200	The five fibre instances are installed by hand — they do not synthesize through the `relCurve`
201	`def` barrier, exactly as `Pic0RingDatumEngine` records. -/
202	theorem htriv_of_pic0 (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hg : genus C = 0)
203	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (overSpec k B))
204	    (h : picEtAffineEquiv C B (lam : picEt C (overSpec k B))
205	      = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass))
206	    (p : PrimeSpectrum B) :
207	    (D.baseChange p.asIdeal.ResidueField).cechPicClass = 1 := by
208	  haveI : IsIntegral (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
209	    instIsIntegralBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
210	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1
211	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
212	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
213	  haveI : QuasiCompact
214	      (relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :=
215	    instQuasiCompactBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
216	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule
217	      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).moduleKSheaf p.asIdeal.ResidueField) 0) :=
218	    instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C p.asIdeal.ResidueField
219	  haveI : Module.Finite p.asIdeal.ResidueField (Sheaf.HModule

271	`exists_datum_pic0_presentation` upgrades it to the datum form. -/

277	        = PicEtAff.unit C B (relPicMk C (overSpec k B) D.cechPicClass) :=

282	
283	This is the form the earlier statements should have had: the only hypotheses left are the
284	membership itself, that the class comes from `relPic` (`hz`), the covering datum and the

10	/-!
11	# The algebra→scheme seam for two-chart ℙ¹ coboundaries
12	
13	The pure-algebra layer (`Picard/LaurentTwoChartCoboundary.lean` and the `Algebra/Laurent*`
14	files) characterises `laurentCoboundaryUnits A`, the coboundary subgroup of the abstract
15	two-chart datum `Polynomial.toLaurent`, `rightChart A` on the Laurent overlap ring
16	`LaurentPolynomial A`.  A scheme consumer of `Scheme.cechPic_eq_one_of_forall_presenting_coboundary`
17	instead holds `Scheme.twoChartCoboundaryUnits V`, the coboundary subgroup of the scheme
18	restriction maps `X.resHom` on `Γ(X, V₀ ⊓ V₁)ˣ`.
19	
20	Both are literally `TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits` of the respective restriction ring homs
21	(`Scheme.twoChartCoboundaryUnits` unfolds to it by definition, `LaurentTwoChartCoboundary.lean`
22	and `TwoChartCechPicTrivial.lean:71`).  So an **identification of the two data** — ring
23	isomorphisms of the two chart section rings with `A[t]` and of the overlap section ring with
24	`A[T;T⁻¹]`, intertwining the scheme restrictions with `toLaurent`/`rightChart` — transports
25	coboundary membership between them.  This file is that seam: it consumes the identification as
26	hypotheses (the base-changed `ℙ¹_A` two-chart cover that realises them is the remaining scheme
27	build) and hands back the scheme-side `twoChartCoboundaryUnits` membership the criterion wants.
28	
29	Nothing here assumes the identifying isomorphisms are anything in particular, and nothing here
30	uses a new hypothesis on the ring `A`: it is the naturality of `cechCoboundaryUnits`
31	(`TruncExpCech.mem_cechCoboundaryUnits_map_iff`) instantiated at the two Laurent chart maps.
32	
33	## Main declarations
34	
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_twoChartCoboundaryUnits_iff_laurent` — given the chart identification
36	  data, a scheme overlap unit is in `twoChartCoboundaryUnits V` iff its `A[T;T⁻¹]ˣ` image is in
37	  `laurentCoboundaryUnits A`.
38	-/
39	
40	set_option autoImplicit false
41	
42	universe u
43	
44	open CategoryTheory
45	
46	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
47	
48	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] {X : Scheme.{u}} {V : Bool → X.Opens}
49	
50	/-- **The algebra→scheme coboundary seam.**
51	
52	Suppose the two-chart cover `V` of `X` is Laurent-identified over `A`: ring isomorphisms
53	`γ₀ : Γ(X, V false) ≃+* A[t]`, `γ₁ : Γ(X, V true) ≃+* A[t]` of the two chart section rings and
54	`γ₀₁ : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true) ≃+* A[T;T⁻¹]` of the overlap section ring, intertwining the
55	scheme restrictions `X.resHom` with the two Laurent chart maps
56	(`Polynomial.toLaurent`, `rightChart A`):
57	
58	* `hres₀ : γ₀₁ ∘ resHom(inf_le_left) = toLaurent ∘ γ₀`;
59	* `hres₁ : γ₀₁ ∘ resHom(inf_le_right) = rightChart A ∘ γ₁`.
60	
61	Then a scheme overlap unit `u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ` is a two-chart coboundary iff its
62	image `Units.map γ₀₁ u : (A[T;T⁻¹])ˣ` is a Laurent coboundary.  Composed with the landed
63	`mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff_general`, this reads the scheme-side coboundary condition off
64	the exponent-zero normal form of the transported Laurent unit — with no new hypothesis. -/
65	theorem mem_twoChartCoboundaryUnits_iff_laurent
66	    (γ₀ : Γ(X, V false) ≃+* Polynomial A) (γ₁ : Γ(X, V true) ≃+* Polynomial A)
67	    (γ₀₁ : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true) ≃+* LaurentPolynomial A)
68	    (hres₀ : (γ₀₁ : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true) →+* LaurentPolynomial A).comp
69	        (X.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false))
70	      = (Polynomial.toLaurent : Polynomial A →+* LaurentPolynomial A).comp
71	        (γ₀ : Γ(X, V false) →+* Polynomial A))
72	    (hres₁ : (γ₀₁ : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true) →+* LaurentPolynomial A).comp
73	        (X.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true))
74	      = (rightChart A).comp (γ₁ : Γ(X, V true) →+* Polynomial A))
75	    (u : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true)ˣ) :
76	    u ∈ Scheme.twoChartCoboundaryUnits V
77	      ↔ Units.map (γ₀₁ : Γ(X, V false ⊓ V true) →+* LaurentPolynomial A).toMonoidHom u
78	          ∈ laurentCoboundaryUnits A := by
79	  have h :=
80	    TruncExpCech.mem_cechCoboundaryUnits_map_iff
81	      (X.resHom (inf_le_left : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V false))
82	      (X.resHom (inf_le_right : V false ⊓ V true ≤ V true))
83	      (Polynomial.toLaurent : Polynomial A →+* LaurentPolynomial A) (rightChart A)
84	      γ₀ γ₁ γ₀₁ hres₀ hres₁ u
85	  exact h.symm
86	
87	end AlgebraicGeometry

# THE FIELD-TEST LAYER OF THE `pic⁰` VANISHING, AT GENUS `0`

`Picard/Pic0VanishingAffineReduction.lean` reduces the `∀ T` binder of the degree-zero Picard
vanishing to an equivalent statement about test *rings*.  This file closes the **field** case
of that statement at genus `0`, for an arbitrary base field and every field extension.

The content is `RiemannRoch/GenusZeroDegreeTrivial.eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one`
transported to the carrier `relPicDeg` actually reads: `relPic C (overSpec k L)`, the Čech
Picard group of the base-changed curve modulo classes pulled back from the base.

## Why the base change is the whole plumbing cost

`relPicDeg L` is a homomorphism out of `relPic C (overSpec k L)`, whose representatives are
Čech classes on `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left` — the curve base-changed to `L`, *not* `C`.  So the
`χ = 1` hypothesis has to hold at the base-changed curve at **every** field extension, and
`genus C = 0` is a statement about `C` over `k`.

That transport is landed and needs no new cohomology: `finrank_h0_baseField` and
`finrank_h1_baseField_eq_genus` (`Cohomology/H1BaseFieldInvariance.lean:353,363`) compute both
Betti numbers of the base-changed curve, and `h0_moduleKSheaf` gives `h⁰ = 1` over `k`.  Then
`χ = h⁰ - h¹ = 1 - genus C = 1`.

Why *these* lemmas: they are stated at `(C ⊗ overSpec k L).left.moduleKSheaf L` under
`instOverBaseChange` (`Curve/BaseChangeInstances.lean:74`), which is the key `relPicDeg`'s
degree stack consumes, so no transport is needed.

**RETRACTED CLAIM, and it was published as a prohibition.**  An earlier version of this
paragraph said that going through `chi_moduleKSheaf` at the bundled `baseChangeBundle C L`
gives the same object under a different `Over` instance and that "the resulting `chi` terms do
not unify — measured".  **That is false.**  The bundled route closes at default heartbeats once
a `change` to the bundled spelling precedes the `simpa`; what was actually measured was one
`simpa` failing *without* that step, i.e. a fact about a tactic call, restated as a fact about
two objects.  `Curve/P1DegreeZeroTrivial.lean` (pic-g) does it the bundled way at `ℙ¹`.  Both
routes work; this one is not the only one and nothing here forecloses the other.

## What this does NOT do

* **It is not the vanishing.**  After the affine reduction the surviving obligation quantifies
  over test *rings*; a field is a ring, so this is one instance of it and not the statement.
  The general-ring case needs a fibrewise-to-global argument (cohomology and base change) that
  this tree does not have, and nothing here supplies it.
* **It says nothing at positive genus**, and it does not claim to: at `genus C > 0` the
  hypothesis `genus C = 0` simply fails, and this file exhibits no positive-genus curve.
* **It does not produce a `JacobianData`** on its own.  The producer
  `jacobianData_of_overSpec_subsingleton` wants the ring-level hypothesis; the field case does
  not discharge it.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChange_eq_one_of_genus_zero` — `χ(𝒪) = 1` at the

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.TwoChartCechPicTrivial
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Algebra.LaurentUnits
8	
9	/-!
10	# THE ℙ¹ TWO-CHART COBOUNDARY SUBGROUP OVER A DOMAIN IS EXACTLY THE CONSTANTS
11	
12	`Picard/TwoChartCechPicTrivial.lean` reduces triviality of a chart-trivial Picard class on a
13	two-chart cover to the purely algebraic question *are the overlap units all coboundaries?*.  This
14	file answers that question for the pinned ℙ¹ chart data — overlap ring `A[t,t⁻¹]`, chart rings
15	`A[t]` and `A[t⁻¹]` — over a **domain** `A`, in both directions:
16	
17	> a Laurent unit is a coboundary **iff** it is `C c` for a unit `c` of `A`.
18	
19	## Read this before using it: the answer is NO, and that is the correct answer
20	
21	The criterion of the previous file asks for *every* overlap unit to be a coboundary.  Over a
22	domain that is **false**, and this file is what proves it false: `T 1 = t` is a unit of
23	`A[t,t⁻¹]` and is *not* a coboundary, because `t` is a unit of neither chart ring
24	(`Polynomial.isUnit_iff`: a unit of `A[t]` over a domain is a constant).
25	
26	That is not an obstruction to the route — it is the statement that
27	
28	```
29	Pic(ℙ¹_A)  =  A[t,t⁻¹]ˣ ⧸ (A[t]ˣ · A[t⁻¹]ˣ)  =  ℤ,
30	```
31	
32	the classical computation, with the class of `t` generating.  The consequence for the
33	representability route is the useful one, and it is a *sharpening* rather than a defeat: the
34	hypothesis that must be supplied is not "all overlap units are coboundaries" but "the overlap
35	unit presenting **this** class has exponent zero" — i.e. exactly a degree-zero condition, which
36	is what `pic0Subgroup` cuts out in the first place.  A lane pricing the ring case should price
37	that, not the false universal form.
38	
39	## Where `IsDomain` is used, and where it is not
40	
41	* the **forward** direction (a coboundary is a constant) uses it, through
42	  `Polynomial.isUnit_iff` on each chart — over a general ring `A[t]` has non-constant units
43	  (`1 + εt` with `ε² = 0`) and the direction genuinely fails;
44	* the **converse** (a constant unit is a coboundary) uses **no** hypothesis on `A`: `C c` is the
45	  left chart's image of the polynomial unit `C c`.  The `omit` marker records that.
46	
47	`Algebra/LaurentUnits.lean` already proves the necessity of `IsDomain` for the Laurent unit
48	classification as a theorem rather than a remark; this file is the two-chart-cohomological
49	consequence of that classification.
50	
51	## Main declarations
52	
53	* `AlgebraicGeometry.rightChart` — the second chart map `A[t] → A[t,t⁻¹]`, `t ↦ T (-1)`.  The
54	  two charts of ℙ¹ are both polynomial rings; they differ by which of `t, t⁻¹` they send `X` to.
55	* `AlgebraicGeometry.C_unit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits` — a constant unit is a coboundary, over
56	  any commutative ring.
57	* `AlgebraicGeometry.eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits` — over a domain, a coboundary is a
58	  constant unit.
59	* `AlgebraicGeometry.mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff` — the two together, as an `iff`.
60	* `AlgebraicGeometry.not_tUnit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits` — `t` is **not** a coboundary over a
61	  domain: the generator of `Pic(ℙ¹_A) = ℤ`, and the refutation of the universal form of the
62	  criterion's hypothesis.  `IsDomain` alone suffices — a separate `Nontrivial` binder was
63	  redundant (the `overlappingInstances` linter caught it), which is worth noting because the
64	  statement *is* false at the zero ring for the trivial reason that `t = 1` there.
65	-/
66	
67	set_option autoImplicit false
68	
69	universe u
70	
71	open CategoryTheory
72	
73	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
74	
75	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
76	
77	/-- The second ℙ¹ chart map `A[t] → A[t,t⁻¹]`, sending the coordinate to `t⁻¹`.  The first is
78	mathlib's `Polynomial.toLaurent` (`X ↦ T 1`); both chart rings are polynomial rings, and the
79	cover is recorded by *which* Laurent monomial the coordinate goes to. -/
80	noncomputable def rightChart (A : Type u) [CommRing A] :
81	    Polynomial A →+* LaurentPolynomial A :=
82	  Polynomial.eval₂RingHom LaurentPolynomial.C (LaurentPolynomial.T (-1))
83	
84	@[simp]
85	lemma rightChart_X : (rightChart A) Polynomial.X = LaurentPolynomial.T (-1) := by
86	  simp [rightChart]
87	
88	@[simp]
89	lemma rightChart_C (c : A) : (rightChart A) (Polynomial.C c) = LaurentPolynomial.C c := by
90	  simp [rightChart]
91	
92	/-- The coboundary subgroup of the ℙ¹ overlap units: products of images of the two chart unit
93	groups.  Abbreviation for the `TruncExpCech` subgroup at the two chart maps. -/
94	noncomputable abbrev laurentCoboundaryUnits (A : Type u) [CommRing A] :
95	    Subgroup (LaurentPolynomial A)ˣ :=
96	  TruncExpCech.cechCoboundaryUnits
97	    (Polynomial.toLaurent : Polynomial A →+* LaurentPolynomial A) (rightChart A)
98	
99	/-- **A constant unit is a coboundary** — no hypothesis on `A`.
100	
101	`LaurentPolynomial.C c` is the left chart's image of the polynomial unit `Polynomial.C c`. -/
102	theorem C_unit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits (c : Aˣ) :
103	    (Units.map (LaurentPolynomial.C : A →+* LaurentPolynomial A).toMonoidHom c)
104	      ∈ laurentCoboundaryUnits A := by
105	  have h : Units.map (LaurentPolynomial.C : A →+* LaurentPolynomial A).toMonoidHom c
106	      = Units.map (Polynomial.toLaurent : Polynomial A →+* LaurentPolynomial A).toMonoidHom
107	          (Units.map (Polynomial.C : A →+* Polynomial A).toMonoidHom c) := by
108	    ext; simp
109	  rw [h]
110	  exact TruncExpCech.unitsMap_mem_cechCoboundaryUnits_left _ _ _
111	
112	/-- **Over a domain, a coboundary is a constant unit.**
113	
114	Both chart unit groups consist of constants (`Polynomial.isUnit_iff`, which needs `IsDomain`),
115	and both chart maps send `Polynomial.C c` to `LaurentPolynomial.C c`, so a product of chart
116	images is `C` of the product.
117	
118	This is the direction that fails over a general ring: `1 + εt` is a unit of `A[t]` whenever
119	`ε² = 0`, so `A[t]ˣ` is bigger than the constants there. -/
120	theorem eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits [IsDomain A] {u : (LaurentPolynomial A)ˣ}
121	    (hu : u ∈ laurentCoboundaryUnits A) :
122	    ∃ c : A, IsUnit c ∧ (u : LaurentPolynomial A) = LaurentPolynomial.C c := by
123	  obtain ⟨v, w, hvw⟩ := TruncExpCech.mem_cechCoboundaryUnits.mp hu
124	  obtain ⟨cv, hcv, hv⟩ := Polynomial.isUnit_iff.mp v.isUnit
125	  obtain ⟨cw, hcw, hw⟩ := Polynomial.isUnit_iff.mp w.isUnit
126	  refine ⟨cv * cw, hcv.mul hcw, ?_⟩
127	  rw [← hvw]
128	  change Polynomial.toLaurent (v : Polynomial A) * (rightChart A) (w : Polynomial A)
129	    = LaurentPolynomial.C (cv * cw)
130	  rw [← hv, ← hw]
131	  simp [rightChart, map_mul]
132	
133	/-- **THE CHARACTERIZATION**: over a domain, the coboundary subgroup is exactly the constants.
134	
135	So the two-chart Čech Picard group of `ℙ¹_A` is the Laurent units modulo the constants, which by
136	`LaurentPolynomial.unitsEquiv` (`Aˣ × ℤ`) is `ℤ`. -/
137	theorem mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits_iff [IsDomain A] {u : (LaurentPolynomial A)ˣ} :
138	    u ∈ laurentCoboundaryUnits A
139	      ↔ ∃ c : A, IsUnit c ∧ (u : LaurentPolynomial A) = LaurentPolynomial.C c := by
140	  refine ⟨eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits, ?_⟩
141	  rintro ⟨c, hc, hu⟩
142	  obtain ⟨cu, rfl⟩ := hc
143	  have h : u = Units.map (LaurentPolynomial.C : A →+* LaurentPolynomial A).toMonoidHom cu :=
144	    Units.ext hu
145	  rw [h]
146	  exact C_unit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits cu
147	
148	/-- **`t` IS NOT A COBOUNDARY** over a nontrivial domain — the generator of
149	`Pic(ℙ¹_A) = ℤ`, and the refutation of the *universal* form of the criterion's hypothesis in
150	`Picard/TwoChartCechPicTrivial.lean`.
151	
152	If it were, it would be a constant by `eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits`; but `T 1` has its
153	support in degree `1`, and comparing coefficients at `0` gives `0 = c` while at `1` gives
154	`1 = 0`.
155	
156	Recorded as a theorem rather than a remark because the previous file's criterion asks for *every*
157	overlap unit to be a coboundary, and a consumer must know that that hypothesis is FALSE here — so
158	the thing to supply is a degree-zero condition on the presenting unit, not the universal form. -/
159	theorem not_tUnit_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits [IsDomain A] :
160	    LaurentPolynomial.tUnit (R := A) 1 ∉ laurentCoboundaryUnits A := by
161	  intro hmem
162	  obtain ⟨c, hcu, hc⟩ := eq_C_of_mem_laurentCoboundaryUnits hmem
163	  rw [LaurentPolynomial.tUnit_coe] at hc
164	  -- `T 1 = C 1 * T 1` and `C c = C c * T 0`, so `exp_unique` gives `1 = 0`
165	  have h : (LaurentPolynomial.C (1 : A) * LaurentPolynomial.T (1 : ℤ))
166	      = LaurentPolynomial.C c * LaurentPolynomial.T (0 : ℤ) := by
167	    rw [map_one, one_mul, LaurentPolynomial.T_zero, mul_one]
168	    exact hc
169	  exact absurd (LaurentPolynomial.exp_unique (one_ne_zero (α := A)) h) one_ne_zero
170	
171	end AlgebraicGeometry

6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Curve.P1H1Vanishing
7	import AlgebraicJacobian.RiemannRoch.GenusZeroDegreeTrivial
8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.H1BaseFieldInvariance
9	
10	/-!
11	# A DEGREE-ZERO PICARD CLASS ON `ℙ¹_K` IS TRIVIAL, FOR EVERY FIELD EXTENSION `K/k`
12	
13	`RiemannRoch/GenusZeroDegreeTrivial.lean` proves `classDeg K L = 0 → L = 1` from `χ(𝒪_X) = 1`
14	at an abstract curve `X` over `K`.  This file instantiates it at `ℙ¹`, which needs `χ = 1` at
15	the *base-changed* curve for every extension `K/k` rather than only over the base field.
16	
17	**READ THE STATUS NOTE BELOW BEFORE CITING THIS FILE.**  An earlier version of this paragraph
18	attributed the "not instantiated at any concrete curve" observation to a note *inside*
19	`GenusZeroDegreeTrivial.lean`.  That is **false** — grep finds no such phrase there, at the
20	commit that wrote it or at HEAD.  The observation came from inbox `I-1616`, a message from the
21	lane that wrote that file, and a docstring is the wrong place to have laundered an inbox
22	message into a citation.
23	
24	## STATUS: this file is a COROLLARY LAYER, not an independent result
25	
26	Measured by a fresh-context audit (`I-1633`), and it is the honest framing: **all four
27	declarations below follow from `Picard/Pic0VanishingFieldGenusZero.lean` alone**, which landed
28	seven minutes earlier and is general in the curve.  `chi_baseChange_eq_one` is one application
29	of that file's `chi_moduleKSheaf_baseChange_eq_one_of_genus_zero` to
30	`P1.genus_asOver_eq_zero`; I re-verified the subsumption myself rather than take it on report.
31	
32	What is genuinely not duplicated is `eq_of_classDeg_eq_baseChange` — no
33	`Injective (classDeg …)` statement exists elsewhere in the tree — and the value of the rest is
34	that the specialisation at `ℙ¹` is spelled out where a reader of the `ℙ¹` material will find it.
35	That is a convenience, and it should not be quoted as new mathematics.
36	
37	## Why the base-changed curve and not just `ℙ¹_k`
38	
39	The consumer is the `∀ T` binder of the `pic⁰` vanishing.  `pic0Subgroup C T` is cut out by
40	`degAt` at *every field point* `t : overSpec k K ⟶ T` (`Picard/Pic0Functor.lean:107`), and
41	`degAt` is read through `relPicDeg K` on `relPic C (overSpec k K)`, which is a quotient of
42	`CechPic ((C ⊗ overSpec k K).left)` — the Čech Picard group of the curve base-changed to `K`.
43	So the field-point content of the vanishing is a statement about `ℙ¹_K` for every `K`, and a
44	computation over `k` alone does not touch it.
45	
46	## The composite, and where each input comes from
47	
48	`genus (baseChangeBundle C K) = genus C` is base-field invariance of the genus
49	(`Cohomology/H1BaseFieldInvariance.lean:373`), and `χ(𝒪) = 1 - genus`
50	(`RiemannRoch/ChiCurve.lean:148`).  At `C = P1.asOver k` the genus is `0`
51	(`Curve/P1H1Vanishing.lean:187`), so `χ = 1` at `ℙ¹_K` for **every** `K`.  Feed that to
52	`eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one`.
53	
54	Nothing here is new mathematics; all four inputs were landed and unconnected.  The reason it
55	was worth a file is that the composite is what turns a theorem about an abstract curve
56	carrying a `χ` hypothesis into a fact about an object this project has built.
57	
58	## What this does NOT do
59	
60	It does **not** discharge `∀ T : Over (Spec k), Subsingleton (pic0Subgroup (P1.asOver k) T)`,
61	and the gap is not a quantifier shuffle.  `pic0Subgroup C T` at a general test `T` consists of
62	classes on `C ⊗ T` whose restriction to every *field* point has degree zero; this file says
63	each of those restrictions is trivial, which is **fibrewise triviality**, not triviality.
64	Concluding the class itself is trivial is the descent step — for `T = overSpec k A` it is
65	`Pic(ℙ¹_A) ≅ Pic(A) × ℤ`, cohomology and base change — and it is untouched here.
66	
67	Recorded because the distance is easy to misread: the field case being closed makes the ring
68	case look like bookkeeping, and it is not.  In particular a chart-by-chart argument does not
69	extend from fields to rings, and the reason is worth separating into what is measured here and
70	what is quoted from outside:
71	
72	* **measured.** `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic (Polynomial k))` is `inferInstance` for a *field*
73	  `k` (through `NormalizedGCDMonoid`), which is what makes the charts of `ℙ¹_k` have trivial
74	  Picard group.  The same query for a general `[CommRing A]` **fails**, and it fails even
75	  given `Subsingleton (CommRing.Pic A)` as a hypothesis.  So the instance that carries the
76	  field argument is simply absent over a ring.
77	* **measured.** `grep -rli` over all of mathlib returns **zero** files matching `seminormal`
78	  and zero matching `traverso`; the `suslin` hit is Suslin's theorem in descriptive set
79	  theory, and every `quillen` hit is the model-structure Quillen.  So no route through that
80	  literature is available in the library as it stands.
81	* **quoted, not verified here.** That `Pic(A[t]) = Pic(A)` holds *exactly* for seminormal `A`
82	  is Traverso–Swan, mathematics from outside this formalization.  Nothing in this tree proves
83	  it or its failure, and the sentence is here to explain why the instance search above is not
84	  merely missing a lemma — not as a formalized no-go.
85	
86	## Main declarations
87	
88	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.chi_baseChange_eq_one` — `χ(𝒪) = 1` on `ℙ¹_K` for every field
89	  extension `K/k`.
90	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_baseChange` — **a degree-zero Čech Picard
91	  class on `ℙ¹_K` is trivial**, and `classDeg_eq_zero_iff_baseChange`, the iff.
92	* `AlgebraicGeometry.P1.eq_of_classDeg_eq_baseChange` — the degree determines the class, which
93	  is the shape a degree-cut-out subgroup consumes.
94	-/

97	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
98

100	
101	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
102	
103	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
104	
105	namespace P1
106	
107	variable (k : Type u) [Field k] (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K]
108	
109	/-- **`χ(𝒪) = 1` on `ℙ¹_K`, for every field extension `K/k`.**
110	
111	`χ = 1 - genus` at any curve, and the genus is a base-field invariant, so this is
112	`genus (P1.asOver k) = 0` transported along `K/k`.  This is the input
113	`eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one` needs and the one its author flagged as not
114	elaborated at a concrete curve. -/
115	theorem chi_baseChange_eq_one :
116	    Sheaf.chi (((P1.asOver k) ⊗ overSpec k K).left.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 := by
117	  haveI : IsProper (baseChangeBundle (P1.asOver k) K).hom :=
118	    instIsProperSndLeft (P1.asOver k) K
119	  haveI : SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (baseChangeBundle (P1.asOver k) K).hom :=
120	    instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionSndLeft (P1.asOver k) K
121	  haveI : GeometricallyIrreducible (baseChangeBundle (P1.asOver k) K).hom :=
122	    instGeometricallyIrreducibleSndLeft (P1.asOver k) K
123	  have hg : genus (baseChangeBundle (P1.asOver k) K) = genus (P1.asOver k) :=
124	    genus_baseField (P1.asOver k) K
125	  have h0 : genus (P1.asOver k) = 0 := P1.genus_asOver_eq_zero k
126	  have hchi := chi_moduleKSheaf (baseChangeBundle (P1.asOver k) K)
127	  rw [hg, h0] at hchi
128	  -- `(baseChangeBundle C K).left` is `(C ⊗ overSpec k K).left` by `rfl`; the two spellings
129	  -- differ only in which one typeclass resolution keys the `Over` instance on.
130	  change Sheaf.chi ((baseChangeBundle (P1.asOver k) K).left.moduleKSheaf K) = 1
131	  simpa using hchi
132	
133	/-- **A degree-zero Čech Picard class on `ℙ¹_K` is trivial**, for every field extension
134	`K/k`.
135	
136	The instantiation `GenusZeroDegreeTrivial` was missing: its `χ(𝒪_X) = 1` hypothesis is
137	discharged at this carrier by `chi_baseChange_eq_one`. -/
138	theorem eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_baseChange
139	    (L : ((P1.asOver k) ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic)
140	    (hL : classDeg K L = 0) : L = 1 :=
141	  eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_of_chi_one K (chi_baseChange_eq_one k K) L hL
142	
143	/-- The iff, so `classDeg` is visibly **injective** on `CechPic (ℙ¹_K)` rather than merely
144	having trivial kernel on the nose. -/
145	theorem classDeg_eq_zero_iff_baseChange
146	    (L : ((P1.asOver k) ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic) :
147	    classDeg K L = 0 ↔ L = 1 :=
148	  ⟨eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_baseChange k K L, fun h => by rw [h, classDeg_one]⟩
149	
150	/-- **The degree determines the class on `ℙ¹_K`**: two Picard classes of the same degree are
151	equal.  (Injectivity of `classDeg`, stated on the multiplicative Picard group rather than on
152	`Additive`, which is the spelling every consumer in this tree uses.)
153	
154	This is the form the degree-zero *subgroup* consumes: `pic0Subgroup` is cut out by a degree
155	condition, and a subgroup lying in the kernel of an injective homomorphism is trivial. -/
156	theorem eq_of_classDeg_eq_baseChange
157	    (L L' : ((P1.asOver k) ⊗ overSpec k K).left.CechPic)
158	    (h : classDeg K L = classDeg K L') : L = L' := by
159	  have hdiv : classDeg K (L * L'⁻¹) = 0 := by
160	    rw [classDeg_mul, classDeg_inv, h]
161	    omega
162	  exact mul_inv_eq_one.mp (eq_one_of_classDeg_eq_zero_baseChange k K _ hdiv)
163	
164	end P1
165	
166	end AlgebraicGeometry
